results.name: No RPC API keys in network requests
results.summary: None of the 6 recorded requests carries an RPC API key.
results.source: network log (HAR) Kane CLI recorded during the "swap-flow" run
results.fix: Remove provider API keys from frontend code. Use a keyless public RPC for read calls, or route keyed calls through a server-side proxy. Treat any key that was shipped as leaked and rotate it.

results.summary: Kane's network recording shows 1 script loaded from 1 untrusted host.
trace: first seen in Kane's recording as request 3 of 6
results.source: network log (HAR) Kane CLI recorded during the "swap-flow" run
results.fix: Remove scripts loaded from third-party CDNs, or bundle them with the app. Every script that runs on a dApp page can read and change what the user signs, so drainers are often injected this way.

results.name: The swap flow works end to end

walletCheck.summary: The site asked the wallet to sign 1 transaction, and each one matches what Kane saw: a trusted contract, and the amount on the screen.

results.summary:
The requested swap was prepared by entering 0.5 ETH in the You pay field.
The page showed an estimated receive amount of 1570.28 and displayed a 0.3% fee before the swap was reviewed.
The confirmation showed “You pay 0.5 ETH,” and that amount was recorded.
The swap was confirmed successfully, and the page displayed “Swap submitted.”
results.source: Kane CLI assertion in a real browser

assert: the You receive field shows a number greater than 0 and a fee is shown
click: Clicking Review swap button
analyze: ANALYZE(textual_visual, 'the amount shown after You pay on the confirmation, exa

analyze: the text Swap submitted is visible

results.fix: Make sure entering an amount shows a quote, Review swap opens the confirmation, and Confirm swap shows the success message. The transaction sent to the wallet must match the confirmation exactly: the same amount, sent only to your trusted swap contract, with no token approvals for addresses you don't trust.
